Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL INFORMATION
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referral Reason: Diagnostic testing for Cystic Fibrosis
Clinical Indication: Suspected Cystic Fibrosis

TEST PERFORMED
Targeted CFTR Gene Sequencing Panel

TEST DESCRIPTION
Targeted DNA sequencing analysis was performed on selected regions of the CFTR gene (NM_000492.4). The test includes sequencing of 10 CFTR exons (4, 6a, 7, 10-13, 19-21) and partial intron 19. This panel covers pathogenic variants accounting for:
• 87.65% of disease-causing variants in individuals of Caucasian ancestry
• 56.41% of disease-causing variants in individuals of South Asian ancestry
• 76% of disease-causing variants worldwide

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. Target regions were amplified by PCR and sequenced bidirectionally using Sanger sequencing. Sequence data was analyzed against the CFTR reference sequence NM_000492.4.

RESULTS
Gene: CFTR (Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator)
Result: No pathogenic variants detected in the screened CFTR regions

All analyzed exons showed normal sequence without evidence of pathogenic variants.

TECHNICAL NOTES
• Coverage: All targeted regions achieved >20x coverage with Q30 scores >85%
• Variant detection sensitivity: >99% for single nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions (<20bp) in covered regions
• This screening method yields negative results in approximately 6% of patients with confirmed Cystic Fibrosis

INTERPRETATION
No pathogenic variants were identified in the analyzed regions of the CFTR gene. This negative result does not exclude a diagnosis of Cystic Fibrosis, as this targeted panel does not interrogate all possible disease-causing variants in CFTR.

LIMITATIONS
• This test does not sequence the entire CFTR gene
• Large deletions/duplications and deep intronic variants are not detected by this method
• Variants in non-covered regions will not be identified
• Rare or population-specific variants may not be included in this panel

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
Cystic Fibrosis diagnosis is not confirmed by this genetic test. However, as the test covers only a partial spectrum of CFTR variants, the condition cannot be completely ruled out based on these results alone.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Clinical correlation is recommended. If clinical suspicion for Cystic Fibrosis persists based on symptoms and other diagnostic tests (sweat chloride, pancreatic function), consider referral for comprehensive CFTR variant screening at a specialized laboratory
2. Comprehensive CFTR sequencing including all exons, intron-exon boundaries, and deletion/duplication analysis may identify variants not covered by this panel
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss test results and implications for the patient and family members

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
